defect: While refreshing the stale F1 contract quote during the Step-7 preflight round, the reviewing Alpha re-read the supplier and found the carrier overreached: a fixed-horizon, probability-one statement (and a prescribed countable horizon family) was asserted as one outcome simultaneously covering every compact interval.
correction_basis: Narrowed the refuted implication, the witness and every proof step to the fixed interval [0,1], where the supplier cor-brownian-paths-have-infinite-one-variation-and-finite-quadratic-variation gives uniform dyadic quadratic-variation convergence and infinite total variation on the same probability-one event; the contract entry was regenerated and precheck passes. The defect-ledger row (severity fatal, disposition narrowed) and the reviewing Alpha's report research/phase-2-remaining-27-alpha-d-step7-preflight-repair.md carry the evidence.

defect: While refreshing obsolete shortened F1/F3 quotations during the Step-7 preflight round, the reviewing Alpha found the generator construction omitted u=T, described the pointwise constant-one process as elementary although the required value at time zero is zero, and inferred the empty-set case through complement closure before proving it; the boundary and risk records also charged countable choice to a step that only selects finitely many approximants for each fixed m.
correction_basis: Regenerated the exact Definition quotes, added the terminal-horizon constructions for s>0 and s=0, represented the constant-one L2 class by the elementary one-block process 1_(0,T] modulo the null time-zero slice, proved the empty case directly with zero, and corrected the choice row and the complete risk review to the finite-selection proof. The defect-ledger row (severity fatal, disposition fixed) and the reviewing Alpha's report research/phase-2-remaining-27-alpha-d-step7-preflight-repair.md carry the evidence.

defect: The definition inferred that its canonical energy hitting times were stopping times, and that the stopped energy was bounded pointwise, from continuity holding only almost surely on a filtration explicitly allowed to be noncomplete and non-right-continuous.
correction_basis: Kept the earlier finite-energy construction on raw filtrations but imposed the usual conditions precisely at the localization interface, while retaining the standard almost-sure local-energy class. On the common full-probability event G the energy is finite-valued and continuous on every finite horizon; completeness makes the discrepancy between each hitting-time event and the corresponding measurable energy-level event measurable, so the canonical times are stopping times, increase almost surely to infinity, and bound the stopped energy almost surely. Right-continuity is declared with completeness as the standard convention used by the cited localization sources and inherited by downstream stopping theory.

defect: The torus-classification proof consumed countable-choice-only exponential suppliers without assuming or deriving countable choice, and its lattice induction merely asserted that the projected subgroup remains discrete. The resulting incomplete supplier left the definition's product-of-circles assertion supported circularly.
correction_basis: The theorem now assumes full AC and invokes lem-ac-supplies-countable-and-dependent-choice-for-banach-integration to obtain exactly the countable choice required by its exponential-map and circle-group suppliers; the unused universal-cover dependency was removed. Step 3.2 proves projection discreteness using representatives in a compact cylinder before applying induction, so the exponential-kernel argument establishes the classification independently of the definition's classification sentence. Conrad–Landesman §6.1, Lemma 6.11, Fact 6.12 and Theorem 6.13 gives this exponential/discrete-kernel route; Knapp Corollary 1.103(b)–(c) gives the same quotient-by-a-discrete-subgroup classification.

defect: The purported usual augmentation adjoined only subsets of raw-terminal Brownian null events and explicitly excluded other ambient null events, so it did not supply the complete filtration required by the chosen localization convention and left null-path normalizations potentially nonadapted.
correction_basis: The null ideal now consists of subsets of ambient null events in the completed probability space. The symmetric-difference argument still gives raw representatives, while every ambient null set is now in F_0 and the right-limit construction is both complete and right-continuous, exactly the usual-conditions interface used by localization and Brownian martingale representation.

defect: The theorem retained the obsolete assertion that the usual augmentation need not contain arbitrary ambient null events and justified its random-time normalization by avoiding precisely the completeness now required by the owner-selected split convention.
correction_basis: The statement and F2 now use the repaired complete usual augmentation. The continuous-version exceptional event lies in F_0, so normalizing the random-time values there preserves adaptedness and leaves all almost-sure strong-Markov identities unchanged.

defect: The localized-integral theorem still said that no completeness was assumed and that local energy was pointwise finite, contradicting its repaired direct dependency and leaving the stopping/local-martingale interface on the rejected raw-filtration convention.
correction_basis: The theorem now states the inherited usual-conditions hypothesis and consistently treats local energy and canonical energy bounds as almost-sure assertions. Its finite-energy construction remains unchanged, preserving the owner-selected raw-filtration side of the split.

defect: The stopping theorem still required a pointwise finite-energy representative and claimed that the canonical localizers tend to infinity pointwise, assertions stronger than and inconsistent with the repaired almost-sure local-energy definition.
correction_basis: The theorem now assumes the usual conditions through the local-integrability interface, states finite local energy and exhaustion almost surely, and retains the finite-energy stopping comparison and indistinguishability proof on the resulting common full-probability event.

defect: The Itô-process definition retained the old raw-filtration convention: drift and diffusion energy were required on every path, stopping preserved pointwise integrability, and common energy localizers were said to exhaust pointwise.
correction_basis: The definition now starts at the localization interface under the usual conditions, uses almost-sure finite drift variation and diffusion energy on every finite horizon, gives a measurable finite-value convention for the drift integral, and states common-localizer exhaustion almost surely. This reconciles the scalar and multidimensional Itô conventions consumed downstream.

defect: The shifted Brownian law lived only on cylinder space, but its consumers treated closed-set hitting conditions as measurable events of that law; for uncountable time this measurability did not follow from the cylinder-space definition.
correction_basis: The law is now the pushforward of an everywhere-continuous normalized Brownian version to canonical continuous path space with its compact-open Borel sigma-algebra. Coordinate generation proves random-element measurability, and closed-set hitting by a fixed finite time is a closed path-space event, so the scalar and planar exit events are well typed.

defect: The condition definition allowed the empty tree through vacuous perfectness and used an undefined recorded-tree length, so the empty pair became an absorbing condition and the intended perfect carrier and canonical zero coordinate were unavailable.
correction_basis: Restricted nontrivial conditions to nonempty perfect nowhere-dense trees, defined the recorded height as the maximum node length, and adjoined a separate distinguished weakest condition for canonical embeddings. Shelah Definition 7.7 says the witness is a perfect nowhere-dense tree, while Claim 7.11 explicitly uses the minimal zero coordinate; Roslanowski–Shelah state the general weakest-condition convention.

defect: The local sweetness interface admitted forcing preorders without a distinguished weakest condition, although the amalgamation and canonical-copy constructions use a weak filler coordinate; this licensed the terminal-antichain counterexample in the fatal receipt.
correction_basis: Required a distinguished weakest condition, allowed it to lie outside the dense sweetness domain, and stated that canonical copies and amalgams fill unused coordinates with it. This is exactly the forcing convention used by the cited sweetness sources and supplies the carrier interface already used by the escalated consumers.

defect: The measured interpretation demanded DC even though its consumers supply only Countable Choice and the underlying local coin-measure proof uses DC solely to derive that weaker principle.
correction_basis: Stated Countable Choice at the measured-domain interface and made the reduction explicit: after step 1.2 of the published dyadic-coding lemma, the pullback construction uses only the countable-choice hypotheses of the Lebesgue suppliers, and the completion theorem itself assumes Countable Choice. This narrows only the measure interface and does not purport to repair the separate relative-L[x] complexity gap.

defect: The local definition imposed an externally transitive ZFA+AC ground, although Corson's construction starts with a model of ZFA+AC and the relative-consistency consumer supplies only the corresponding internal model.
correction_basis: Removed the external transitivity requirement and stated that the ordered metric structure, automorphism group, supports and hereditarily symmetric interpretation are all computed internally in the ZFA+AC ground. Corson explicitly begins with a model of ZFA+AC, and the standard Fraenkel–Mostowski setup confirms this interface.

defect: The Step-7 proof repair added a dependency from the root-systems page to a later highest-weight-page proposition, closing a two-page dependency cycle even though the converse proof needed only earlier root-system facts.
correction_basis: L4 now takes root spanning, reducedness, reflection invariance and integrality from the earlier theorem on semisimple roots, while [L5] supplies the simple-root basis and nonsingularity already used elsewhere in the proof. The simple-coroot basis conclusion follows from alpha_j(h_i)=a_ij. The Step-7 ideal and weight-space semisimplicity repair is unchanged.

defect: The classification theorem redundantly cited a later highest-weight-page Euclidean-root proposition, supplying the reverse page edge that kept the root-systems/highest-weight cycle alive.
correction_basis: L1 now cites the earlier semisimple-root theorem for the root decomposition, spanning, reducedness, reflection invariance and Cartan integrality actually used. The Step-7 correction that separates root-system existence from classification remains intact, and no conclusion was weakened.

defect: The compact-page theorem cited the later real-forms page merely for the canonical conjugation on an explicitly displayed complexification, creating a compact-to-real-forms page edge.
correction_basis: L7 now defines sigma(U+iV)=U-iV directly and records bracket preservation, involutivity and the fixed algebra from the complex-bilinear bracket and uniqueness of real and imaginary parts. The Step-7 sign correction sigma(e_alpha)=-f_alpha and the compact SU(2) construction are untouched.

defect: The Step-7 repair made the compact classification page depend on later compact-real-form existence and conjugacy theorems, completing the compact/real-forms page cycle although the required compact structure can be proved from earlier Serre data.
correction_basis: For two existing compact groups, compact-normalized simple-root triples and the Serre presentation now give an isomorphism intertwining the two standard conjugations. For realization, the proof defines the conjugation on the Serre algebra, proves -B(X,kappa Y) positive by the Cartan/root decomposition and Weyl automorphisms, and realizes the group as Aut(k)^0. The Step-7 finite-kernel compact-cover correction remains unchanged.

defect: The root-data theorem cited the later real-forms canonical-conjugation proposition while lifting marked Serre generators, adding a second compact-to-real-forms edge that was unnecessary for the proof.
correction_basis: L5 records the standard conjugation of the displayed compact complexification directly, and L6 uses the compact-normalized Serre generators already supplied by the analytic Weyl theorem. The Step-7 repair of the character-lattice quotient and central kernel is unchanged, so the root-data realization and uniqueness claims retain their full strength.

defect: The repaired hyperbolic example used compact-page Haar measure to prove maximal compactness, creating the examples-to-compact edge that completed the compact/real-forms/examples cycle.
correction_basis: Step 3.2 already proves that G is connected semisimple with finite center, that Theta is a global Cartan involution and that its fixed group is K. Step 4.1 now applies the same real-forms page's maximal-compact corollary directly. The Step-7 direct Killing-form trace computation for every n>=2 is unchanged.

defect: After the three-page cycle was removed, depcheck exposed a nested real-forms/examples cycle: this real-forms false statement depended on the companion-page polar example, while the companion page necessarily requires the real-forms page.
correction_basis: Step 1.1 now proves SL_2(R) connected by an elementary QR path and verifies all hypotheses of the already-cited global Cartan theorem. Step 2.1 obtains the polar diffeomorphism from that theorem and precomposes the circle cover. The Step-7 universal-cover and integral-weight nonlinearity repairs remain intact.

defect: The supplier asserted the relative L[x] complexity and null-union argument without a choice-free predecessor certificate, and its displayed relation did not explicitly enforce the strict first-code order on G times G.
correction_basis: Relativized the canonical definition-code order using well-founded countable L[x]-level and exact predecessor certificates obtained from canonical least Skolem witnesses. The new formula is false off G times G and on the diagonal, is Sigma-one-two of x, and completed Tonelli/Fubini now yields the null-union dichotomy without measuring the exceptional vertical sections.

defect: The capture supplier invoked weak-choice coin measure and Borel--Cantelli without establishing those interfaces in ZF, and its infinite slalom union needed a finite-subset argument for the advertised cardinal bound.
correction_basis: Constructed canonical coin content directly from prefix-free cylinder counts, proved tail nullity by explicit open covers, and removed zero-content traces with canonically least finite covers and summable errors; the proof explicitly identifies the relatively open removed union and verifies that null removal preserves positive closed content. Finite pattern counting and least finite witnesses give the sharp slalom bound.

defect: The rapidity proof depended on the repaired relative-L[x] supplier and passed from the null union to an open set of measure below one through an overbroad dyadic-measure citation rather than a valid weak-choice regularity argument.
correction_basis: After the repaired null-code lemma supplies a completed-null union, place it inside a Borel null hull. Inner regularity applied to the hull's complement gives a positive compact set, whose open complement contains the union and has measure below one. The block construction now also uses the dependency's exact first-differing-prefix-length convention and assigns those lengths to the blocks (n_(i-1),n_i].

defect: The downstream inaccessible-in-L proof applied the rapidity theorem after proving measurability only for A(x), although that theorem requires measurability of A(x joined with r) uniformly for every real r.
correction_basis: For each real r, the repaired null-code lemma makes A(x joined with r) Sigma-one-two relative to that joined parameter. Boldface Sigma-one-three measurability therefore supplies every required instance, and the proof now explicitly passes this uniform family to the rapidity theorem before deriving the nonmeasurable Sigma-one-three filter contradiction.

defect: The proof falsely replaced every nontrivial Vogan-diagram involution by the identity and then used an incomplete painted-vertex count, omitting and miscounting classical and exceptional real forms.
correction_basis: The proof now retains nontrivial diagram involutions under Borel--de Siebenthal reduction and delegates the finite case analysis to Knapp Theorem 6.105, including both directions, the twelve exceptional noncompact noncomplex forms and the sole normalized duplicate. Etingof's independent type-by-type account confirms the retained outer classes.

defect: The downstream classical table used matrices of the wrong sizes for so*(2n) and sp(p,q), asserted false compactness reasoning, and did not obtain exhaustion from a correct classification supplier.
correction_basis: The proposition now uses the 2n-by-2n matrix J_n for so*(2n), the 2n-by-2n Hermitian matrix diag(S_pq,S_pq) for sp(p,q), verifies the fixed loci, and invokes the repaired classification for exhaustion. It also records compact and split endpoints, ranks and all stated low-rank duplicates, including so*(8) isomorphic to so(6,2).

defect: The definition treated suspension isomorphisms and cofiber connecting maps as independent data, so a sign-twisted connector still satisfied the written interface and destroyed the claimed reduced/unreduced inverse correspondence.
correction_basis: Every cofiber connector is now defined, rather than independently chosen, by delta_f=q_f^* sigma for the fixed sphere-first cofiber convention. Exactness and morphisms use that normalization, matching the explicit cone-boundary construction in Loizides and the reduced/unreduced framework in Davis--Kirk.

defect: The theorem is the only draft consumer of the pairing lemma and it consumed the false clause directly: its Statement, fact A3 and proof steps advertised the cohomological AHSS as a bigraded ring on every page from E1 onward, a claim the escalated interval witness refutes at E1^{1,0}, so the theorem asserted a strictly stronger multiplicative structure than the mathematics supplies.
correction_basis: The theorem now states multiplicativity from the second page on. It cites the pairing lemma only for the typed first-page pairing, its Leibniz rule for d1 and its descent to E2, and for the ring products, the derivation property, the ring isomorphism E_{r+1} = H(E_r,d_r) and the identification of the E2 product with the graded cup product on which independence from the cellular approximation of the diagonal rests; the first-page statement is explicitly restricted to the pairing and its Leibniz rule, with the lemma's six-segment witness recorded as the reason no E1 ring is asserted. Sources: Dugger section 3.1 with Theorem 3.4 and Miller Lecture 29, printed pp. 100-101.

defect: The supplier was phrased through a ground-model construction whose proof did not state an arbitrary internal ZFA+AC interface, leaving both BPI separation theorems without a valid bridge from the possibly externally ill-founded model supplied by first-order completeness.
correction_basis: The theorem is now formulated and proved internally in an arbitrary model of ZFA+AC. Internal Choice constructs the prime-ideal compactum; stabilizer-coset control proves joint continuity; internal extreme amenability supplies a fixed prime ideal; and finite support plus elementwise hereditary symmetry place it in the permutation interpretation. This exact arbitrary-ground interface composes with the tagged ZFA interpretations in both BPI consistency proofs without assuming external transitivity.
